core_research_thesis: Design and optimization of a high-performance, safe, and long-lasting battery through the integration of electrochemistry, materials science, electrical engineering, and thermodynamics
proven_facts: The Nernst equation relates electrode potential to concentration
The Butler-Volmer equation describes electrode kinetics
Fick's laws govern diffusion in electrolytes
Ohm's law applies to electrical resistance in batteries
Thermodynamic laws dictate energy conversion efficiency and entropy
critical_unanswered_unknowns: Optimal electrode material composition for high capacity and cycle life
Effect of electrolyte additives on battery performance and safety
Influence of cell architecture on thermal management and efficiency
Robustness of battery management systems to faults and failures
Long-term degradation mechanisms and lifespan prediction

proposed_testable_hypotheses.Solid-state electrolytes improve safety: Thermal runaway testing and leakage current measurement
proposed_testable_hypotheses.Thermally managed cells reduce degradati: Accelerated life testing and thermal imaging
proposed_testable_hypotheses.Machine learning-based control algorithm: Experimental validation using real-time data and model predictive control

failure_modes_and_risks: Electrode material degradation and capacity loss
Battery management system failures and software bugs
required_empirical_data_inputs: Electrode material properties and characterization data
Battery management system logs and performance data
